title: Giáo dục tài chính bắt buộc
prompt: Some people think that financial literacy, such as budgeting, saving and understanding loans, should be a compulsory subject in secondary schools. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
sample:
In many countries, young adults leave school without knowing how to budget, save or borrow wisely. I strongly agree that financial literacy should be a compulsory subject in secondary schools, because it equips students with skills that affect their entire lives.

First, money management is a practical necessity that traditional subjects rarely cover. Graduates must sign rental contracts, compare loan offers and decide how much to save for retirement, yet many have never read an interest-rate table. Without guidance, they become easy targets for high-interest credit cards or online scams. A short, well-designed course on budgeting, compound interest and credit would reduce such mistakes, and the cost to schools would be small compared with the debt problems it could prevent.

Second, teaching these ideas early builds lasting habits. Teenagers who learn to track their spending and set savings goals are more likely to continue doing so as adults. Moreover, financial education can narrow inequality. Children from wealthy families often learn about investing at home, whereas those from poorer households receive no such advice. A compulsory subject would give every student the same basic knowledge, regardless of background.

Critics argue that the timetable is already overcrowded and that parents should be responsible for this topic. However, not all parents are financially confident themselves, and a new subject can replace some less useful content rather than add to the workload. Maths lessons, for example, could use real household budgets and loan calculations instead of abstract exercises.

Schools that already run such programmes often find that students become noticeably more confident when discussing money with their families, which shows the practical value of the subject.

In conclusion, I firmly believe that compulsory financial education benefits both individuals and society, and governments should introduce it without delay.
notes_vi:
Dạng: Opinion (To what extent do you agree?). Chọn lập trường rõ ngay mở bài (ở đây: strongly agree) và giữ nhất quán.
Dàn ý: (1) Mở bài: paraphrase đề + nêu quan điểm. (2) Thân bài 1: lý do thực tế - sinh viên mới ra trường phải thuê nhà, vay tiền, tiết kiệm hưu trí nhưng không được dạy. (3) Thân bài 2: hình thành thói quen sớm + giảm bất bình đẳng giữa gia đình giàu và nghèo. (4) Thân bài 3: phản biện ý 'chương trình đã quá tải / là việc của cha mẹ' rồi bác lại. (5) Kết bài: nhắc lại quan điểm.
Cụm từ hay: compulsory subject, financial literacy, an easy target for scams, build lasting habits, narrow inequality, regardless of background, without delay.
Lỗi hay gặp: viết 'the finance' thay vì 'financial literacy/ education'; quên nêu quan điểm ở mở bài; liệt kê ý chung chung không có ví dụ cụ thể; dùng 'Firstly, Secondly' máy móc mà không phát triển ý (mỗi đoạn cần ý chính + giải thích + ví dụ).
Mẹo band 7+: có đoạn nhượng bộ/phản biện ngắn (Critics argue... However...).

title: Điện thoại thông minh cho trẻ em
prompt: Some people believe that children under the age of 14 should not be allowed to own a smartphone. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
sample:
Smartphones have become almost unavoidable in modern life, and many children receive one as soon as they start secondary school. Although these devices have some benefits, I largely agree that children under fourteen should not own one, because the risks to their health and development outweigh the advantages.

The main reason is that young teenagers lack the self-control to use phones sensibly. Social media apps are designed to be addictive, and children who spend hours scrolling often sleep less, exercise less and struggle to concentrate in class. Several studies have also linked heavy phone use among adolescents to anxiety and low self-esteem, partly because of constant comparison with other people's lives online. Delaying ownership gives children time to mature before facing these pressures.

Furthermore, an unrestricted phone exposes children to harmful content and to strangers. Even with parental controls, it is difficult for adults to monitor every message or video. Cyberbullying, in particular, follows children home, so that school problems no longer end when the bell rings. A family computer in a shared room, by contrast, is much easier to supervise, and it teaches children that technology is a tool to be used for a purpose rather than a constant companion.

Admittedly, phones help parents stay in touch with their children and can be useful in emergencies. However, this need can be met by a basic handset that only makes calls and sends texts, which avoids most of the dangers described above. Likewise, children can learn digital skills through supervised use of school laptops rather than through personal devices.

In conclusion, while some form of communication device is reasonable, I believe that full smartphone ownership should wait until children are older and better prepared to handle it.
notes_vi:
Dạng: Opinion - 'largely agree' (đồng ý phần lớn) là lập trường an toàn, cho phép nhượng bộ một chút.
Dàn ý: (1) Mở bài: nêu bối cảnh + largely agree. (2) Thân bài 1: trẻ thiếu tự chủ -> nghiện mạng xã hội, ngủ ít, kém tập trung, lo âu. (3) Thân bài 2: nội dung độc hại, người lạ, bắt nạt trực tuyến. (4) Thân bài 3: nhượng bộ (liên lạc, khẩn cấp) rồi đưa giải pháp thay thế: điện thoại cơ bản, laptop của trường. (5) Kết bài.
Cụm từ hay: outweigh the advantages, lack self-control, be designed to be addictive, low self-esteem, parental controls, cyberbullying, a basic handset, supervised use.
Lỗi hay gặp: dùng 'children under 14 years old' lặp đi lặp lại - hãy dùng đại từ/từ đồng nghĩa (young teenagers, adolescents); nhầm 'affect' (động từ) và 'effect' (danh từ); viết 'many studies show' mà không nói rõ chung chung - nên dùng 'Several studies have linked...' để an toàn.
Mẹo: dùng 'Admittedly... However...' để thể hiện lập luận hai chiều.

title: Trách nhiệm bảo vệ môi trường
prompt: Some people say that protecting the environment is the responsibility of governments rather than individuals. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
sample:
Climate change, plastic waste and air pollution now dominate the news. While individuals can certainly contribute, I largely agree that governments carry the main responsibility for protecting the environment, because only they have the power to change entire systems on a large scale.

First, governments can make rules that apply to everyone. Industry produces far more emissions than households, and factories will not voluntarily cut pollution if doing so reduces their profits. Laws that set emission limits, tax carbon or ban single-use plastics force companies to change and create a level playing field. When a ban on plastic bags was introduced in several countries, for instance, usage fell sharply within months, something that decades of public appeals had failed to achieve.

Second, governments control the infrastructure that determines people's choices. Citizens cannot use public transport if no reliable buses or trains exist, nor can they recycle if the city has no collection system. Investment in renewable power, railways and waste processing therefore has a much greater impact than individual decisions to switch off a light or carry a reusable bottle.

That said, individuals are not free from responsibility. Consumer demand influences what businesses sell, and personal habits such as reducing food waste or buying less fast fashion add up across millions of households. Education campaigns can also encourage these habits and build public support for stronger government policy, which shows that the two levels of action support each other. Governments, after all, are far more likely to act when they know that voters care about the issue.

In conclusion, although personal action matters, the scale of environmental problems means that governments must lead through regulation and investment, with individuals playing a supporting role.
notes_vi:
Dạng: Opinion về trách nhiệm (government vs individuals). Không cần chọn cực đoan; 'largely agree' + thừa nhận vai trò cá nhân là ổn.
Dàn ý: (1) Mở bài: nêu vấn đề + quan điểm. (2) Thân bài 1: chính phủ ban hành luật áp dụng cho tất cả (giới hạn khí thải, thuế carbon, cấm nhựa dùng một lần) - ví dụ cấm túi nilon. (3) Thân bài 2: chính phủ kiểm soát hạ tầng (giao thông công cộng, thu gom rác, năng lượng tái tạo). (4) Thân bài 3: vai trò bổ trợ của cá nhân (tiêu dùng, giảm lãng phí thực phẩm). (5) Kết bài.
Cụm từ hay: carry the main responsibility, emission limits, tax carbon, single-use plastics, a level playing field, renewable power, consumer demand, add up across millions of households.
Lỗi hay gặp: viết 'the environment is polluted by factories' mà không đưa giải pháp; dùng 'government' không có mạo từ/ số nhiều (the government / governments); lạc đề sang liệt kê các vấn đề môi trường thay vì trả lời câu hỏi 'ai chịu trách nhiệm'; ví dụ quá chung chung - hãy nêu một ví dụ cụ thể như cấm túi nhựa.

title: Phòng bệnh hay đầu tư bệnh viện
prompt: Some people believe that governments should spend more money on promoting healthy lifestyles, while others think the priority should be building more hospitals and providing better medical treatment. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
sample:
Health care is one of the largest items in any national budget, and there is ongoing debate about how it should be spent. While some argue for investment in hospitals and treatment, others favour campaigns that encourage healthy living. I will discuss both views before explaining why I lean towards prevention.

Those who support spending on hospitals make a reasonable point. Patients who are already ill need immediate and effective treatment, and no campaign can help someone with a heart attack or a broken leg. In many developing regions, people still travel for hours to reach a clinic, and shortages of doctors and equipment cost lives. Modern facilities and well-trained staff are therefore essential for any society.

On the other hand, supporters of prevention believe that it is more efficient to stop diseases before they begin. Illnesses linked to diet, smoking and inactivity, such as diabetes and lung disease, account for a large share of hospital admissions. Public campaigns, healthy school meals and sports facilities are relatively cheap, yet they can reduce the number of patients over time. Countries that have restricted tobacco advertising and taxed sugary drinks, for example, have seen consumption of these products fall.

In my opinion, a balance is necessary, but I believe prevention deserves greater priority. Hospitals will always be overwhelmed if the population continues to develop avoidable diseases, whereas healthier citizens need fewer treatments, live longer and remain productive. The money saved could then be used to improve the quality of care for those who truly need it.

In conclusion, although treatment is indispensable, promoting healthy lifestyles offers better long-term value, and governments should give it a larger share of the health budget.
notes_vi:
Dạng: Discussion + give your opinion. Phải (a) trình bày công bằng cả hai quan điểm, (b) nêu ý kiến riêng rõ ràng, tốt nhất ở mở bài và đoạn kết luận.
Dàn ý: (1) Mở bài: paraphrase, nói sẽ bàn cả hai và nghiêng về phòng bệnh. (2) Thân bài 1: quan điểm xây bệnh viện - bệnh nhân cần điều trị ngay, thiếu bác sĩ/thiết bị ở vùng xa. (3) Thân bài 2: quan điểm nâng cao lối sống lành mạnh - bệnh liên quan ăn uống, hút thuốc, ít vận động; chiến dịch rẻ hơn; ví dụ thuế đồ uống có đường. (4) Thân bài 3: ý kiến cá nhân - cần cân bằng nhưng ưu tiên phòng bệnh. (5) Kết bài.
Cụm từ hay: national budget, healthy lifestyles, immediate treatment, account for a large share of, hospital admissions, avoidable diseases, long-term value, deserve greater priority.
Lỗi hay gặp: chỉ bàn một phía hoặc quên nêu ý kiến riêng; dùng 'the first view is... the second view is...' quá khô cứng; nhầm 'prevent' và 'prevention'; viết 'healthy lifestyle' không có 'a/ promote' đi kèm.
Mẹo: đặt ý kiến cá nhân ở đoạn riêng để giám khảo dễ thấy (Task Response).

title: Làm việc tại nhà hay văn phòng
prompt: Some people prefer to work from home, while others believe that working in an office is better. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
sample:
Since the pandemic, many employees have discovered that they can do their jobs from their living rooms. Some people see remote work as the future, whereas others still prefer the traditional office. This essay will discuss both sides, and I will argue that a mixture of the two works best.

Working from home has clear attractions. Employees save the time and money they would spend commuting, which can amount to several hours a week, and they can organise their day more flexibly, for example by taking a break to collect children from school. Many people also report fewer interruptions, so that tasks requiring deep concentration are completed faster. Companies benefit as well, since they can reduce the cost of renting large offices.

However, the office offers advantages that are hard to reproduce online. Face-to-face contact makes teamwork and spontaneous conversations easier, and these informal exchanges often produce new ideas. Younger staff, in particular, learn quickly by watching experienced colleagues, which is difficult over video calls. Moreover, some workers find that the boundary between work and personal life disappears at home, leading to isolation and longer hours.

In my view, the most sensible arrangement is a hybrid model in which employees work at home for part of the week and meet colleagues on fixed days. This approach keeps the flexibility that people value while preserving the cooperation and sense of belonging that a workplace provides. It also allows managers to adapt the rules according to the nature of each job, so that creative teams and customer service staff can each follow the pattern that suits them.

In conclusion, both options have genuine strengths and weaknesses, and I believe that combining them offers the best outcome for staff and employers alike.
notes_vi:
Dạng: Discussion + opinion. Ý kiến cá nhân không nhất thiết phải chọn một phe: 'mô hình kết hợp (hybrid)' là lập trường hợp lệ nếu được giải thích rõ.
Dàn ý: (1) Mở bài: bối cảnh sau đại dịch + nói sẽ ủng hộ mô hình kết hợp. (2) Thân bài 1: ưu điểm làm việc tại nhà - tiết kiệm thời gian/ tiền đi lại, linh hoạt, ít bị gián đoạn, công ty giảm chi phí thuê văn phòng. (3) Thân bài 2: ưu điểm văn phòng - làm việc nhóm trực tiếp, trao đổi ngẫu hứng sinh ý tưởng, nhân viên trẻ học từ đồng nghiệp, ranh giới công việc - đời tư rõ ràng. (4) Thân bài 3: ý kiến riêng - hybrid. (5) Kết bài.
Cụm từ hay: work from home / remote work, commute, flexibly, deep concentration, face-to-face contact, a sense of belonging, hybrid model, adapt to the nature of each job.
Lỗi hay gặp: dùng 'work at home' thay cho 'work from home'; nhầm 'commute' (danh từ/động từ) với 'communicate'; viết 'In my opinion, I think' (thừa); chỉ liệt kê ưu - nhược mà không có ví dụ; dùng 'bored' thay vì 'boring' khi mô tả công việc.
Lưu ý: dùng 'whereas / while' để đối chiếu hai quan điểm ngay mở bài.

title: Ùn tắc và ô nhiễm đô thị
prompt: In many large cities, traffic congestion and air pollution are getting worse. What problems do these cause, and what solutions can you suggest?
sample:
As more people move to big cities, roads are becoming overcrowded and the air is increasingly polluted. These trends create serious problems for residents and for the economy, but there are practical measures that governments can take to address them.

The most obvious problem is the damage to public health. Exhaust fumes from millions of vehicles contain fine particles that cause asthma, heart disease and other illnesses, and children and the elderly are particularly vulnerable. Congestion also wastes time and money. Commuters may spend two hours a day stuck in traffic, which reduces productivity, raises stress and increases fuel consumption. Companies, in turn, face higher costs for delivering goods, and these costs are eventually passed on to customers.

One effective solution is to improve public transport. If metros and buses are fast, cheap and frequent, many drivers will leave their cars at home. Several cities that have invested heavily in underground networks have noticeably reduced traffic on their main roads. Dedicated bus lanes and safe cycle paths can further encourage people to choose cleaner alternatives.

A second measure is to make driving more expensive in crowded areas. Congestion charges, higher parking fees and limits on older, polluting vehicles discourage unnecessary journeys, and the revenue can be used to fund public transport. In addition, planners should create new business districts and housing in smaller towns, with good transport links, so that jobs and people are spread more evenly rather than concentrated in a single centre.

In conclusion, congestion and pollution harm both health and the economy, but better public transport, charges on driving and balanced urban planning can substantially reduce both problems.
notes_vi:
Dạng: Problem-solution. Cần trả lời đủ hai phần: các vấn đề (problems) và giải pháp (solutions). Mỗi giải pháp nên gắn với một vấn đề đã nêu.
Dàn ý: (1) Mở bài: paraphrase + nói sẽ nêu vấn đề và giải pháp. (2) Thân bài 1 - vấn đề: sức khoẻ (bụi mịn, hen suyễn, bệnh tim) và kinh tế (mất thời gian, tăng chi phí vận chuyển, căng thẳng). (3) Thân bài 2 - giải pháp 1: cải thiện giao thông công cộng, làn xe buýt riêng, đường dành cho xe đạp. (4) Thân bài 3 - giải pháp 2: phí ùn tắc, phí đỗ xe, hạn chế xe cũ; quy hoạch đô thị phân tán sang các thị trấn nhỏ. (5) Kết bài.
Cụm từ hay: traffic congestion, exhaust fumes, fine particles, be particularly vulnerable, pass on costs to customers, dedicated bus lanes, congestion charge, urban planning, concentrated in a single centre.
Lỗi hay gặp: nhầm 'pollution' (không đếm được) - viết 'a pollution'; dùng 'traffic jams' quá thân mật so với 'congestion'; chỉ nêu giải pháp chung chung kiểu 'government should do something' mà không nói cụ thể là gì; thiếu liên kết giữa vấn đề và giải pháp.

title: Tội phạm ở người trẻ
prompt: Youth crime is increasing in many cities. What problems does this cause for society, and what can be done to reduce it?
sample:
Crimes such as theft, vandalism and street violence committed by teenagers are rising in many urban areas. This trend worries both residents and officials, because it affects public safety and wastes young people's potential. In this essay I will outline the main problems and suggest some solutions.

The most immediate problem is the fear and loss that crime brings to communities. Shop owners suffer financial damage, residents feel unsafe walking at night, and neighbourhoods with a reputation for crime often lose businesses and investment. For the young offenders themselves, a criminal record can close doors to education and employment, which may push them towards further offences and create a cycle that is difficult to break. The cost of policing and imprisonment also falls on taxpayers.

To tackle this, governments should focus on prevention. Many teenagers turn to crime out of boredom or because they lack positive role models, so funding youth clubs, sports programmes and after-school activities would give them constructive alternatives. Schools can also help by identifying pupils who are often absent or struggling, and by offering counselling and mentoring before problems escalate. Support for families facing poverty is equally important, since an unstable home life is a common background factor.

When offences do occur, the response should combine accountability with rehabilitation. Instead of sending first-time offenders to prison, where they may meet hardened criminals, courts could require community service and training programmes. Such punishments make young people repair the harm they have caused while teaching them skills for a lawful career, and evidence suggests that they lower the chances of reoffending.

In conclusion, youth crime damages communities and young lives alike, but investment in prevention and rehabilitation can reduce it effectively.
notes_vi:
Dạng: Problem-solution. Hai phần đều cần được phát triển; giải pháp nên cụ thể và khả thi.
Dàn ý: (1) Mở bài: nêu xu hướng tội phạm vị thành niên tăng + sẽ nêu vấn đề và giải pháp. (2) Thân bài 1 - vấn đề: nỗi sợ và thiệt hại của cộng đồng, cửa hàng bị phá, khu phố mất đầu tư; người trẻ có tiền án khó học/ xin việc -> vòng luẩn quẩn; gánh nặng chi phí cho người nộp thuế. (3) Thân bài 2 - giải pháp phòng ngừa: câu lạc bộ thanh thiếu niên, thể thao, hoạt động sau giờ học; trường học phát hiện sớm học sinh trốn học; hỗ trợ gia đình nghèo. (4) Thân bài 3 - giải pháp xử lý: lao động công ích, đào tạo nghề thay cho nhà tù với người phạm lần đầu. (5) Kết bài.
Cụm từ hay: youth crime, vandalism, a criminal record, a cycle that is difficult to break, role models, constructive alternatives, accountability, rehabilitation, community service, reoffend.
Lỗi hay gặp: nhầm 'crime' (tội phạm nói chung, đếm được hạn chế) với 'criminal' (người phạm tội); viết 'punish them more severely' làm giải pháp duy nhất - dễ bị coi là thiếu chiều sâu; dùng 'young people' quá nhiều lần nên thay bằng teenagers, juveniles, young offenders; thiếu liên kết giữa nguyên nhân gốc và giải pháp.

title: Mai một ngôn ngữ và văn hoá truyền thống
prompt: Many traditional languages and customs are disappearing as the world becomes more globalised. What problems does this cause, and how can they be solved?
sample:
Every year, several languages fall silent and old customs fade as younger generations adopt global trends. This loss is more serious than it may appear, and it is possible for communities and governments to slow it down.

The first problem is that a language carries knowledge that cannot be fully translated. Local words describe plants, medicines, weather and farming methods that people have observed over centuries, and when the last speakers die, this understanding disappears with them. Second, traditions give people a sense of identity and belonging. Young people who feel disconnected from their roots may suffer from a weaker sense of community, while societies as a whole become less diverse and therefore less interesting and creative.

One solution is to make cultural heritage part of education. Schools in minority regions could teach local languages alongside the national one and organise lessons on traditional crafts, music and stories. When children learn these skills in a positive, enjoyable way, they are more likely to value them as adults. Governments can support this with funding for teacher training and teaching materials.

Technology can also play a helpful role. Communities can record elders telling stories, build online dictionaries and publish videos or podcasts in their own language, which makes tradition attractive to a generation that spends much of its time online. In addition, festivals and tourism, if managed responsibly, create an economic reason to preserve crafts and performances, so that practising a tradition can become a viable career rather than a hobby.

In conclusion, losing languages and customs impoverishes humanity, but education, digital tools and sustainable cultural events can keep them alive for future generations.
notes_vi:
Dạng: Problem-solution (chủ đề văn hoá - toàn cầu hoá). Cần giải thích vì sao đây là 'vấn đề', không chỉ mô tả hiện tượng.
Dàn ý: (1) Mở bài: nêu hiện tượng ngôn ngữ/ phong tục mai một + sẽ nêu vấn đề và giải pháp. (2) Thân bài 1 - vấn đề: mất tri thức bản địa (dược liệu, nông nghiệp, thời tiết), mất bản sắc và cảm giác gắn kết, xã hội kém đa dạng. (3) Thân bài 2 - giải pháp 1: đưa di sản văn hoá vào giáo dục (dạy tiếng địa phương, nghề thủ công, âm nhạc). (4) Thân bài 3 - giải pháp 2: công nghệ (ghi âm người già kể chuyện, từ điển trực tuyến, video/podcast) + lễ hội và du lịch có trách nhiệm tạo động lực kinh tế. (5) Kết bài.
Cụm từ hay: traditional customs, cultural heritage, sense of identity and belonging, disconnected from their roots, minority regions, impoverish, a viable career, sustainable.
Lỗi hay gặp: viết 'culture traditional' sai trật tự từ (phải là 'traditional culture'); nhầm 'custom' (phong tục) với 'costume' (trang phục); dùng 'globalization' nhưng liệt kê sang lợi ích kinh tế lạc đề; nêu giải pháp 'people should protect culture' quá chung - cần hành động cụ thể (ai làm, làm gì).

title: Công ty đa quốc gia
prompt: Multinational companies, such as fast-food chains and clothing brands, now operate in almost every country. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?
sample:
It is now common to see the same restaurants, shops and brands in cities on different continents. This growth of multinational companies has brought both benefits and drawbacks, but in my opinion the disadvantages are more significant than the advantages.

The main advantage is economic. Large companies create jobs, pay taxes and often bring new technology and management skills to the countries where they invest. A foreign factory, for example, may employ thousands of workers in an area with few other opportunities, and nearby suppliers can expand to meet its needs. Consumers also benefit from a wider choice of products at lower prices, because global firms enjoy economies of scale.

Nevertheless, there are serious disadvantages. Local businesses often cannot compete with the marketing budgets and low prices of international giants, and small shops, family restaurants and traditional producers may close as a result. Profits are frequently sent abroad instead of being reinvested locally, so the economic gain is smaller than it first appears. Furthermore, some multinationals have been criticised for paying low wages or ignoring environmental rules in poorer countries, where regulation is weak.

A cultural cost should also be considered. As identical brands spread, local food, clothing and entertainment lose ground, and cities begin to look alike. This homogenisation reduces diversity and can make younger people believe that foreign products are superior to their own heritage.

In conclusion, multinational companies provide employment and affordable goods, but the harm they can do to local enterprises, workers' conditions and cultural diversity is greater, so governments should regulate them more carefully and give priority to protecting local producers.
notes_vi:
Dạng: Advantages/Disadvantages + 'Do the advantages outweigh the disadvantages?'. Với câu hỏi 'outweigh' PHẢI nêu rõ bên nào nặng hơn ngay mở bài và nhắc lại ở kết bài.
Dàn ý: (1) Mở bài: nêu hiện tượng + 'the disadvantages are more significant'. (2) Thân bài 1 - lợi ích: tạo việc làm, nộp thuế, chuyển giao công nghệ/ kỹ năng quản lý; người tiêu dùng có nhiều lựa chọn, giá rẻ nhờ lợi thế quy mô. (3) Thân bài 2 - bất lợi kinh tế: doanh nghiệp nhỏ địa phương không cạnh tranh nổi, lợi nhuận chuyển ra nước ngoài, lương thấp và lơ là môi trường ở nước nghèo. (4) Thân bài 3 - bất lợi văn hoá: đồng nhất hoá, giảm đa dạng. (5) Kết bài.
Cụm từ hay: multinational companies, bring new technology, economies of scale, local businesses, be reinvested locally, weak regulation, homogenisation, lose ground, cultural diversity.
Lỗi hay gặp: liệt kê quá nhiều ý ngắn mà không phát triển; mở bài không nói bên nào nặng hơn (mất điểm Task Response); nhầm 'advantage of' với 'advantage over'; dùng 'a lot of' lặp lại thay vì 'a wide range of / numerous'; dùng 'foods' - 'food' không đếm được.

title: Du học nước ngoài
prompt: More and more students choose to complete their university education in a foreign country. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this trend?
sample:
Studying overseas, once a privilege of a few, is now an option for hundreds of thousands of young people. This trend offers significant academic and personal benefits, yet it also involves costs and risks that students should consider carefully.

The most obvious advantage is educational quality. Many top universities are located in a small number of countries, and graduates of these institutions often enjoy better job prospects and higher salaries. Students also improve their language skills dramatically when they must use a foreign language every day, which is a valuable asset in the global job market. Beyond academics, living abroad teaches independence, adaptability and cultural awareness, because students meet people from many backgrounds and learn to solve problems without family support.

On the other hand, studying abroad is expensive. Tuition fees for international students are usually higher than for locals, and accommodation, flights and living costs add to the total, so many families need to borrow money or use up their savings. There is also an emotional price. Homesickness, loneliness and culture shock can affect students' health and results, particularly in the first months when friendships have not yet formed.

A further drawback concerns the home country. When talented young people stay abroad after graduation, their own nation loses skills that it has helped to develop, a problem often called brain drain. Students who do return may also find it difficult to readjust to local conditions or to find work that matches their expectations.

In conclusion, an overseas degree can open doors and broaden a student's outlook, but high costs, emotional strain and wider social effects mean that it is not the right choice for everyone.
notes_vi:
Dạng: Advantages and disadvantages (không yêu cầu so sánh nặng - nhẹ, nhưng vẫn nên có nhận định cuối).
Dàn ý: (1) Mở bài: paraphrase + nêu sẽ bàn cả lợi và hại. (2) Thân bài 1 - lợi ích: chất lượng đào tạo, cơ hội việc làm/ lương cao hơn, cải thiện ngoại ngữ, tính tự lập và hiểu biết văn hoá. (3) Thân bài 2 - bất lợi cá nhân: học phí và chi phí sinh hoạt cao, nhớ nhà, cô đơn, sốc văn hoá. (4) Thân bài 3 - bất lợi xã hội: chảy máu chất xám, khó tái hoà nhập khi về nước. (5) Kết bài.
Cụm từ hay: study overseas, job prospects, a valuable asset, adaptability, cultural awareness, tuition fees, homesickness, culture shock, brain drain, readjust to.
Lỗi hay gặp: viết 'study abroad in a foreign country' (thừa nghĩa: abroad = ở nước ngoài); nhầm 'tuition' và 'fee'; viết 'a homesick' thay vì 'homesickness'; ví dụ không có số liệu bịa đặt - nên dùng cách nói chung 'often', 'many'; chỉ nêu lợi ích mà quên bất lợi hoặc ngược lại.

title: Giờ làm việc ngày càng dài
prompt: In many countries, people are working longer hours and have less free time than in the past. Why is this happening? Is it a positive or negative development?
sample:
Despite advances in technology that were supposed to make work easier, many employees today feel busier than their parents or grandparents did. This essay will explain the main reasons for this trend and argue that it is mostly a negative development.

There are several causes. Firstly, living costs, especially for housing, have risen faster than wages in many places, so people take extra jobs or overtime to make ends meet. Secondly, competition in the modern economy is intense, and employees fear that leaving the office on time will make them seem less committed, which may affect their chances of promotion. Finally, smartphones and email mean that work follows people home, blurring the line between professional and private time. Messages from a manager at ten o'clock in the evening are hard to ignore.

Some people see long hours as positive because they can lead to higher income and career progress. Ambitious workers may gain skills faster, and companies may become more productive and profitable, which can contribute to national growth. Nevertheless, I believe the drawbacks are far more serious.

Overwork damages health, causing stress, sleep problems and, in extreme cases, serious illness. It also leaves little time for family, friends and hobbies, and relationships suffer when parents rarely see their children. Importantly, research suggests that productivity falls when people are tired, so longer hours do not always mean better results. Societies might therefore be better off adopting shorter working weeks, as a number of pilot schemes have suggested.

In conclusion, rising living costs, competition and technology explain why people work longer, but the damage to health and personal life makes this trend largely negative.
notes_vi:
Dạng: Two-part question (hai câu hỏi riêng). Câu 1 hỏi nguyên nhân (Why), câu 2 hỏi đánh giá (positive or negative). Mỗi câu hỏi cần được trả lời trực tiếp và có đoạn riêng.
Dàn ý: (1) Mở bài: nêu hiện tượng + báo trước sẽ giải thích nguyên nhân và cho rằng xu hướng này tiêu cực. (2) Thân bài 1 - nguyên nhân: chi phí sinh hoạt (nhà ở) tăng nhanh hơn lương nên làm thêm; cạnh tranh gay gắt, sợ bị đánh giá thiếu cam kết; điện thoại/ email khiến công việc theo về nhà. (3) Thân bài 2 - mặt tích cực (thừa nhận ngắn): thu nhập, thăng tiến, năng suất công ty. (4) Thân bài 3 - mặt tiêu cực (chính): sức khoẻ, thiếu thời gian cho gia đình, năng suất giảm khi mệt mỏi, đề xuất tuần làm việc ngắn hơn. (5) Kết bài.
Cụm từ hay: make ends meet, overtime, career progress, blur the line between, work-life balance, overwork, be better off doing, pilot scheme.
Lỗi hay gặp: chỉ trả lời một câu hỏi; trả lời 'positive or negative' mà không chọn rõ phía nào (nếu 'both' thì phải giải thích cân bằng); nhầm 'work' (không đếm được, công việc) với 'job'; viết 'less free times'; dùng 'less' với danh từ đếm được (nên dùng 'fewer').

title: Tin tức qua mạng xã hội
prompt: An increasing number of people get their news from social media rather than from newspapers or television. Why is this happening? Is it a positive or negative development?
sample:
A generation ago, most people learned about world events from the evening bulletin or a daily paper. Today, many simply open an app on their phone. In this essay I will explain the reasons for this change and argue that it is, on balance, a negative development.

The main reason is convenience. Social media is available at any time, free of charge and personalised, so users receive stories that match their interests without searching for them. News also spreads faster there, because ordinary people post videos and comments from the scene within minutes, long before journalists arrive. In addition, younger audiences, who have grown up with smartphones, find traditional formats such as printed newspapers slow and outdated.

There are some positive aspects to this shift. More voices can be heard, including those that mainstream media ignore, and citizens can discuss events directly with each other. Information can also reach remote communities and people in countries with limited press freedom.

Nevertheless, the negative effects seem more important. Social media platforms do not check facts as professional editors do, so rumours and deliberately false stories can spread widely before they are corrected. Moreover, algorithms show users content similar to what they already like, which creates echo chambers where people rarely encounter opposing views. This can increase political division and weaken public trust in reliable institutions. Because many users only read headlines, they may form strong opinions on the basis of incomplete information.

In conclusion, convenience and speed explain the popularity of social media as a news source, but the spread of misinformation and the narrowing of perspectives make this trend more harmful than helpful, and people should check several reliable sources.
notes_vi:
Dạng: Two-part question (Why + positive/negative). Hãy trả lời từng câu trong đoạn riêng, tránh trộn lẫn.
Dàn ý: (1) Mở bài: đối lập thế hệ trước (báo, bản tin tối) và hiện nay (ứng dụng) + nêu quan điểm 'on balance, negative'. (2) Thân bài 1 - nguyên nhân: tiện lợi, miễn phí, cá nhân hoá; tin lan nhanh nhờ người dân đăng video tại hiện trường; giới trẻ thấy báo in chậm, lỗi thời. (3) Thân bài 2 - mặt tích cực: nhiều tiếng nói hơn, tiếp cận vùng xa và nơi hạn chế tự do báo chí. (4) Thân bài 3 - mặt tiêu cực: thiếu kiểm chứng, tin giả lan rộng, thuật toán tạo 'buồng phản hồi' (echo chambers), chỉ đọc tiêu đề, chia rẽ chính trị. (5) Kết bài.
Cụm từ hay: get news from, mainstream media, personalised content, go viral, check facts, misinformation, echo chamber, algorithm, press freedom, on balance.
Lỗi hay gặp: nhầm 'news' (không đếm được) - viết 'a news' / 'many news'; dùng 'social network' và 'social media' lẫn lộn; liệt kê tác hại mà không giải thích cơ chế (vì sao tin giả lan nhanh, vì sao thuật toán gây chia rẽ); quên trả lời câu hỏi 'why' bằng nguyên nhân cụ thể.
